newsitem.title: INDIA: India external debt $92.20 bln at end-March 1996.
newsitem.headline: India external debt $92.20 bln at end-March 1996.

text.p: The Indian government said on Thursday that external debt fell for the first time in the recent past in 1995/96 (April-March), declining to $92.20 billion at end-March 1996 from $99.01 billion one year earlier.

The government said in a statement summarising a report presented to parliament that the nation's debt service ratio -- interest and principal payments as a percentage of exports -- fell to 25.54 at the end of March 1996 from 27.55 one year earlier.

It said the improvements were welcome but the emphasis now had to be on "consolidating existing gains and bringing debt to more manageable levels through sustaining the momentum of export growth, effective management of the existing debt and careful planning of future borrowings".
About three quarters of the decline in debt stock between end-March 1995 and end-March 1996 was attributable to the appreciation of the U.S. dollar against major international currencies, it said.

Concessional debt has remained steady at about 45 percent of total external debt, while the ratio of short-term debt to total debt, which touched 10.2 percent at the end of March 1991, fell to 5.5 percent by the end of March 1996, it said.
